name: Do I need a feasibility assessment before buying land?

mainEntity.name: Should I get a construction feasibility assessment before buying a lot in Los Angeles or nearby cities?
mainEntity.text: Should I get a construction feasibility assessment before buying a lot in Los Angeles or nearby cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Getting a feasibility assessment before buying land is one of the most effective ways to avoid an expensive mistake. In Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood, a lot may look ideal but still be difficult or costly to build on because of slope, access, zoning, utility location, fire-zone requirements, or neighborhood-specific design review. A proper assessment helps answer whether your intended project is realistic, what it may cost, and what approvals could be triggered. That matters especially for luxury homes, additions, and teardown-rebuild projects where the construction budget is only part of the total investment. Buyers should request an assessment before contingencies expire if possible. If the report identifies major red flags, it can support renegotiation, redesign, or walking away from the deal.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. A feasibility assessment can reveal whether the lot can actually support the home, additions, or redevelopment you want. It can uncover hidden issues such as grading limits, easements, setback conflicts, permit complexity, utility constraints, or cost overruns before you close on the property.
